meta.title: Indoor plants for Indian cities (Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru, Kolkata, Pune)
notes: Values are standard horticultural guidelines; always check soil dryness before watering.
Local-name fields are the names used at Indian nurseries (transliterations) except Aloe vera, which has genuine traditional names; verify spellings locally.
Run resolve_images.py to fill image.direct_image_url (and optionally download the files).

watering_every_days.note: Check first: water only when the top 2–3 cm of soil feels dry.

soil.in_simple_words: Loose, sandy soil that drains fast. Water should run out of the pot within seconds.
soil.mix_recipe: 3 parts garden soil + 2 parts coarse sand + 1 part cocopeat (or perlite)

common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are the lower leaves turning yellow, does the soil stay wet for many days, or does the plant base feel soft and smell bad?
solve_it_like_this: Stop watering immediately.
Take the plant out of the pot and cut off all black, soft, smelly roots with clean scissors.
Repot in fresh, dry, well-draining soil in a pot with drainage holes.
Spray or drench with copper oxychloride (3 g per litre of water) or carbendazim (1 g per litre).
Water again only when the top 2–3 cm of soil is dry.

common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Do you see small white cotton-like blobs on stems or under leaves, or sticky leaves?
solve_it_like_this: Isolate the plant from others.
Wipe each bug off with cotton dipped in rubbing alcohol (diluted 1:1 with water).
Spray neem oil (5 ml + 1 ml mild soap per litre) every 7 days for 3 weeks.

common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Do you see fine webbing under the leaves and tiny pale yellow dots on the leaf surface?
solve_it_like_this: Rinse the whole plant under a gentle shower.
Raise the humidity around the plant (pebble tray or regular misting).
Spray neem oil (5 ml + 1 ml mild soap per litre) every 5–7 days for 3 weeks.

common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Do you see brown or black spots, sometimes with a yellow ring, on the leaves?
solve_it_like_this: Cut off badly spotted leaves and throw them away (not in compost).
Stop wetting the leaves; water only the soil.
Move the plant where air moves freely.
Spray copper oxychloride (3 g per litre) every 7–10 days, 2–3 times.

common_problems.problem: Brown, crispy leaf tips or edges
common_problems.do_you_see_this_problem: Are the tips or edges of leaves turning brown and dry?
solve_it_like_this: Check air: keep the plant away from fans, AC vents and heaters.
Use RO, rain or tap water that has stood overnight (tap water salts and fluoride burn tips).
Flush the soil with plain water once a month.
Raise humidity (mist or pebble tray) in dry months.
Trim brown tips with clean scissors; they will not turn green again.
